title: Sectionwise tensor ideal kernel of closed restriction
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $I$ ideal sheaf data on $X$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], and $u:U\to X$ an object of its small etale site. Let $P(I)(U)=\Gamma(U,u^*I.\mathrm{toModules})$ be tensor sections [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial]. Let $l_I(U):\operatorname{ULift}P(I)(U)\to\operatorname{ULift}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ be the lift of the section map of the pullback of the specified ideal inclusion followed by the canonical adjoint structure-module map [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf]. Let $r_I(U)$ be additive restriction [def-sc-etale-additive-structure-restriction] to $U\times_X I.\mathrm{subscheme}$. Then $l_I(U)r_I(U)=0$ and the corresponding kernel fork of additive groups is limiting.

source.place: Proof, Step 1 and its Claim: affine tensor identification with restriction kernels; realized using the already formalized base-change ideal-image and flat-pullback declarations.

proof.text: Construct the structure-module coordinate natural transformation using the normalized restriction equation. Whisker the tensor image of the specified ideal inclusion and these coordinates with the additive universe lift; this is etaleIdealSectionsInclusion, with no choices of arbitrary data.
For an etale structure morphism g, flat module pullback preserves finite limits. Thus the pulled-back ideal inclusion followed by the structure-module isomorphism is monic.

Apply the closed-subscheme base-change ideal-image theorem to I.subschemeι and g. Compare its selected adjunction with the normalized tensor adjunction via leftAdjointUniq. Naturality moves the comparison past the ideal inclusion, so the changed map differs by an isomorphism on the source and has the same image. Pullback symmetry identifies the kernel ideals of pullback.snd and pullback.fst. Since the canonical composite is monic, Subobject.isoOfMkEqMk gives an isomorphism with the kernel ideal module, commuting with inclusion.

Evaluate the inclusion-compatible isomorphism on the top open. The kernel ideal module inclusion is injective and its range is exactly the kernel of restriction to its subscheme. The actual closed immersion factors as toImage followed by this subscheme inclusion. Since toImage is an isomorphism, its global-section map is injective, so the same range is the kernel of the actual restriction.

Corestrict the section map to the concrete additive kernel. Injectivity and the range equality make this corestriction bijective. AddEquiv.ofBijective gives the kernel-group isomorphism; transport AddCommGrpCat.kernelIsLimit along it with IsKernel.isoKernel and apply KernelFork.mapIsLimit for the additive universe lift. This gives the asserted sectionwise limiting fork.

lean.statement:
theorem etaleIdealSectionsInclusion_isKernel {X : Scheme.{u}} (I : X.IdealSheafData)
    (U : X.Etaleᵒᵖ) :
    ∃ h : (etaleIdealSectionsInclusion I).app U ≫
        (etaleAdditiveSheafToLowerStar I.subschemeι).hom.app U = 0,
      Nonempty (IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι (etaleIdealSectionsInclusion I |>.app U) h))
